title: Evidence Orchestration for Model Serving Governance (EOMSG)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable evidence orchestration workflow for Redwood Inference model-serving artifacts. It ties RBAC decisions, audit logs, data residency and retention records, SDLC gates, and incident response artifacts into a single evidence bundle suitable for internal reviews and regulatory audits. The goal is to reduce time-to-evidence from weeks to hours for routine requests and to provide defensible artifacts for escalations.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private model-serving deployments (service names referenced below).
- Covers production control plane and data plane activity: authentication/authorization, configuration changes, model rollouts, inference telemetry, and user data retention events.
- Excludes third-party vendor-only logs (those remain with vendor unless otherwise contracted).

Key services and artifact locations (examples):
- Control plane: redwood-controlplane (terraform state, git tags, CI pipeline runs in CircleCI).
- Serving runtime: redwood-inference-runtime (K8s deployment, deployment manifests, runtime-config).
- Audit ingestion: ingest-audit-pipeline -> ark-s3-logs (S3 bucket with lifecycle policies).
- Key management: kms-redwood / HSM audit outputs (KMIP exports stubbed per customer).
- SIEM: splunk-redwood (index: audit_events), alerting channel: #security-alerts Slack.
- Evidence bundler: evidence-bundler service (internal Lambda) that collates artifacts by request ID.

Control matrix (summary table):
- Authentication: Okta OIDC flows, authn logs from okta-audit (retention 400 days). Evidence: token introspection logs, user directory snapshots.
- Authorization: RBAC policies stored in authz-repo (YAML), evaluated by policy-engine v2. Evidence: policy revision hash, effective role bindings, decision audit trace.
- Configuration change: VCS commits + CI signature. Evidence: commit hash, CI run ID, signed artifact URL.
- Model rollout: model-catalog entries, canary release records. Evidence: model artifact checksum, canary metrics snapshot, fallback policy.
- Data residency & retention: retention-policy registry + S3 lifecycle. Evidence: retention policy id, deletion job audit, legal hold flags.

RBAC mapping and evidence artifacts:
1) Role taxonomy (abbreviated):
   - platform-admin (full control; rarely used; emergency-only approval required)
   - infra-operator (deploy/runtime ops)
   - model-onboarder (model lifecycle create/publish)
   - product-analyst (read-only analytics)
   - customer-support (scoped-read per-customer)

2) Evidence captured per access event:
   - actor id (okta user id)
   - timestamp (ISO8601)
   - evaluated role(s) and applied permissions (policy-engine trace id)
   - decision hash (sha256) and policy revision id
   - request id correlated to invocation (X-Request-ID)

Audit logging and retention policy (operational rules):
- All control-plane authz decisions and API control actions are logged at INFO with structured fields (actor, target, action, decision_id, request_id).
- Data-plane inference events log metadata only: model id, latency_ms, token_count, request_id; PII is never logged.
- Retention targets:
   - Authn/authz decisions: 2 years for enterprise customers; default 400 days for internal.
   - Control-plane config changes: 7 years (legal archival).
   - Inference telemetry (aggregated): 365 days.
   - Raw audit logs in ark-s3-logs: lifecycle transition to cold tier at 180 days, delete after retention period or legal hold.
- Tamper-evidence: all audit S3 objects are immutability-enabled by default (S3 Object Lock) for retention-bound artifacts.

Secure SDLC gates that produce evidence artifacts:
- Pre-commit: linting + policy-as-code checks (opa/unit tests). Evidence: policy-run ID and artifact.
- PR review: required approvers (owners as CODEOWNERS). Evidence: PR link, approvers, signed-off label.
- CI: reproducible build artifact + SBOM generation. Evidence: build ID, artifact checksum, SBOM.json.
- Canary rollout: automated health checks and rollback threshold. Evidence: canary metrics snapshot, canary-decision record.
- Release to prod: release note + release tag + signed release bundle. Evidence: tag, release-notes.md, signed-bundle URL.

Evidence assembly workflow (step-by-step):
1) Intake: compliance engineer opens an Evidence Request in the evidence-bundler UI with scope (customer, timeframe, services). Assign owner.
2) Triage: owner uses automated queries to locate request_ids, commit hashes, and retention-policy ids. If needed, escalate to service owners.
3) Collection: evidence-bundler executes authenticated queries to:
   - pull audit slices from splunk-redwood for timeframe & filters,
   - fetch commit and CI metadata from git + CI,
   - snapshot effective RBAC bindings from authz-repo and policy-engine,
   - confirm S3 object immutability and life-cycle metadata for retention artifacts.
4) Proofing: owner verifies artifacts for completeness: checksums, signatures, and attestation by service owner.
5) Packaging: evidence-bundler composes a Bundle (ZIP) and produces an index.json listing artifacts and canonical hashes.
6) Delivery: store signed bundle in evidence-archive (restricted S3) and record delivery in case-tracker.

Checklist for audit bundles (minimum):
- scope.json (request metadata, timeframe, owner)
- authn_authz_slice.json (auth events and decision traces)
- config_changes.json (git commits + CI IDs)
- model_catalog_snapshot.json (model ids, checksums)
- retention_policy_verification.txt (policy id + S3 lifecycle statements)
- SIEM_alert_history.csv (if relevant)
- attestation.txt signed by service owners and security approver

Incident response integration:
- For security incidents, evidence collection is parallelized and frozen where possible. Steps:
   1) Triage and freeze: incident commander marks evidence request as INCIDENT (priority) and triggers preservation (S3 hold + Splunk export snapshot).
   2) Short-term preservation: evidence-bundler captures live indices and stores them to evidence-incident-buckets (immutable).
   3) Forensic hand-off: provide forensic artifacts to legal and external counsel with chain-of-custody documentation.
- Timelines: critical incident preservation must begin within 2 hours of incident declaration; full bundle delivered to IR lead within 48 hours.

Risk and exceptions process (governance):
- Exceptions exist for transient operational needs (e.g., emergency spool-up) and must be recorded via the Access Exception Request flow. Required fields: owner, risk_acceptor, duration, compensating controls, rollback plan.
- Exception evidence artifacts: approval record, implemented compensating controls (e.g., additional monitoring), post-mortem within 7 days.
- Risk register entry required for exceptions >72 hours or those impacting multiple tenants.

Operational runbook (quick commands & queries):
- Splunk query (example):
  index="audit_events" sourcetype="authz" request_id="{REQUEST_ID}" | table _time, actor, action, target, decision_id, policy_rev
- Git/CI: git show {commit_hash} --name-only; curl -s "https://ci.example.com/builds/{build_id}/artifact" | sha256sum
- Evidence-bundler: POST /api/v1/bundle with body {
      "scope": "{customer}:{from_ts}:{to_ts}",
      "requestor": "{user}"
  } (service requires mTLS and audit token)

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Security Evidence Team (evidence@redwood.com) — maintains bundler and evidence-archive.
- Service owner responsibilities: verify artifacts and provide attestation within SLA (72 hours for routine requests, 24 hours for escalations).
- Escalation path: evidence owner -> security manager -> CISO.

Metrics and SLOs for the evidence pipeline:
- Time-to-first-evidence (median): target < 4 hours for routine bundles.
- Complete-bundle delivery (SLA): 72 hours for non-incident requests; 48 hours for escalations; 7 days legal/complex audits.
- Bundler success rate: 99.5% for automated collections.

Appendix A — Example artifacts and formats:
- scope.json (example): {
  "request_id": "EVID-2026-000123",
  "customer": "acme-corp",
  "timeframe": "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z/2026-07-07T00:00:00Z"
}
- attestation.txt: human-signed statement with name, role, timestamp, and service owner confirmation.

Maintenance and continuous improvement:
- Quarterly tabletop with service owners to validate evidence pipelines and update artifact lists.
- Post-audit retrospective: for every audit >4 hours to assemble, record root causes and remediation backlog.

References and related pages:
- See: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/model-serving-compliance-evidence-playbook-2026 for model-specific evidence items.
- See: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/privileged-role-rotation-and-certification-guideline-2025 for role rotation details.
